newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Kidnappers free Pakistani opposition deputy.
newsitem.headline: Kidnappers free Pakistani opposition deputy.

text.p: A provincial opposition deputy kidnapped in Pakistan's southern province almost two months ago surfaced on Wednesday and said he was freed after he paid part of a demanded ransom.

Pir Mazharul Haq, a member of opposition leader Benazir Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP), told a news conference in Karachi that supporters of Sindh province Chief Minister Liaquat Jatoi had kidnapped him on June 12 and demanded 50 million rupees ($1.23 million) as ranson for his release.
A Sindh government official said police were investigating the matter.

"My kidnappers demanded five crore (50 million rupees) for my release," Haq, deputy leader of opposition in Sindh provincial assembly, said, adding that they had received what he called the first instalment of the ransom. He did not disclose the amount paid.
Haq, a former provincial minister, said he was released overnight somewhere in the province and reached his home in Karachi on Wednesday.
